code_08017F7C.c.why: Wide picture: sub_0801A764 takes the x of a sprite text (the name above a player) as u16, so glyphs left of the console's first column are never drawn. Pass it signed. Drawing only.

Online: the parent corrects each enemy's position on the other machines every 300 frames (five seconds); between corrections every machine moves the enemy by itself, and with a network's latency they drift apart (an enemy seen attacking by one player and standing by another). A third of a second keeps them together (with five enemies that is fifteen short messages a second, well inside what the message channel passes); the message is one short packet now. Parent only, so no machine computes differently for it.

code_080659B0.c.why: Online: declarations of the network layer's message channel for the two patches below (runtime/core/netlink.c, "messages").

Online: the sender of the game's one-time messages (sub_08066720) hands the whole message to the network layer's message channel instead of passing it piece by piece through the block, where every step costs a round trip (runtime/core/netlink.c, "messages"). It ends as the original does after its last step: the block's message bytes say idle after a finished message, sub_0800224C, then the queue is popped. It does not wait for the others to have the message: the channel delivers it in order to everybody, and the game never asks whether the queue is empty (its barriers wait for everybody's token, sub_08067C08). Over a cable (not online) the original code runs.
Online: where the patched sender above rejoins the original to pop the queue.

Online: the receiver task of each player (sub_0806690C) takes that player's next whole message from the network layer's message channel, and puts it where the original assembles the pieces; the dispatch below is the original's. While it waits its acknowledgement byte says idle, as in the original's wait for an announce. Over a cable the original code runs.
Online: where the patched receiver above rejoins the original to act on the message.

Online: the task that starts the sender for the first waiting message (one message, then a frame, then the next) hands every waiting message to the network layer's channel at once instead, so a burst (a map entry, several enemies acting) leaves in the frame it was made. The queue is popped as sub_08066720 pops it.

code_08067B4C.c.why: Online: a player that left a game in progress stays as a standing character (runtime/core/netlink.c, drop) and will never send the token the others wait for before a change of map or scene. sub_080682B8, the game's "does everybody's ring hold this token", counts such a player as ready.
The same: after the scan of one player's ring found nothing (the scan ran to its end), a player that left counts as ready.

code_0807A5D4.c.why: sub_08083AE8 (the message with the sellers' panels that opens the item shop, menu 1) is written against the original 208-byte stack frame: `stack` is the ARM stack pointer, the descriptors, the countdown, the text pointer and the 32-byte text sit at fixed offsets from it, and frameStorage83AE8 is that frame from offset 4. A native build has no such register: the pin was dropped and `stack` was a null pointer, so the function read and wrote addresses 0..0xCF and drew a text that never ends (crash on opening that shop). Give it the frame as a real local.

The same in sub_0808441C (the item made from three others): its 128-byte frame is addressed through the ARM stack pointer. With a null `stack` it lost its own arguments and combined records read from address 0.

Skip scene online: the introduction ends on Start only in a single-player game (gUnk_03002838 is the title menu's choice). While the port's skip is under way (every player voted, runtime/core/scene.c) it ends in any game, through the game's own exit.

code_080443EC.c.why: The same in sub_08048A74 (a town scene with several characters): it takes the address of frame.pos[3] as `stack pointer + 20` for the camera's return to its place. With a null `stack` the eased y went to address 20 and the camera's y stayed 0. `stack` is set so that stack + 20 is frame.pos[3], as in the original frame.
